content: iai-callgrind uses Valgrind Callgrind for instruction-count-based benchmarking — deterministic, no wall-clock noise, one-shot per benchmark. Best for CI regression detection where hardware variance is a concern. Criterion uses statistical wall-clock time analysis (many iterations, outlier rejection) — more representative of real latency but requires stable hardware. Divan is a newer wall-clock harness with ergonomic API but same noise concerns as criterion. For a Rust forecasting library CI: use criterion for primary perf measurement (existing investment) and optionally add iai-callgrind for a noise-free regression gate on hot paths. Bencher.dev is a SaaS/self-hosted platform that integrates with both criterion and iai-callgrind for continuous benchmarking with PR comments.
